cluster_summary: This cluster covers vulnerabilities where credentials (cookies, headers, realms) are improperly handled when crossing trust boundaries such as cross-origin redirects, fetch requests, proxy bypass, and shared client contexts. The root causes include missing credential clearing, incomplete header filtering, incorrect origin references, and unisolated mutable state.
guideline_text: Trace attacker-controlled redirect targets, callback URLs, return URLs, OAuth redirect_uri values, or browser navigation destinations into redirect responses, Location headers, OAuth/OIDC/SAML redirect validation, or browser-followed navigation targets. Report code paths where the redirect target is accepted without constraining the final scheme and destination to trusted browser-safe values. Confirm that the required guard is enforced on the same source-to-sink path before the sensitive effect. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 3 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should validate redirect targets with an explicit safe-scheme and destination allowlist after decoding and normalization.

mechanism.missing_guard: the redirect target is accepted without constraining the final scheme and destination to trusted browser-safe values
mechanism.name: open redirect through unsafe URI scheme validation
mechanism.sink_shape: redirect responses, Location headers, OAuth/OIDC/SAML redirect validation, or browser-followed navigation targets
mechanism.source_shape: attacker-controlled redirect targets, callback URLs, return URLs, OAuth redirect_uri values, or browser navigation destinations
mechanism.typical_fix: validate redirect targets with an explicit safe-scheme and destination allowlist after decoding and normalization

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Ensure all credential sources are cleared when origin changes, including headers and any separate cookies object.
sub_patterns.name: Incomplete credential clearing on redirect
sub_patterns.root_cause: Code fails to remove all sensitive credential sources (Cookie header, Proxy-Authorization header, per-request cookies dictionary) when following a redirect to a different origin.

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Implement an allowlist of safe headers (e.g., Accept, Content-Type, User-Agent) that are permitted to be forwarded during cross-origin redirects.
sub_patterns.name: Denylist-based header filtering on redirect
sub_patterns.root_cause: Code uses a denylist of known sensitive headers or assumes all headers safe, allowing custom authentication headers or common sensitive headers to be forwarded on cross-origin redirects.

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Compute stripAuth based on origin and scheme comparison; conditionally set realm to null and clear future realm/proxyRealm.
sub_patterns.name: Realm propagation without origin validation
sub_patterns.root_cause: No validation that redirect target shares the same origin, and even when stripping Authorization headers, the Realm object with plaintext credentials is still propagated.
